title: The SpatialCellData Object
text: SpatialCellData S4 class central data container phenoscapR. keeps everything experiment one object: validity method guarantees matrices, coordinates, metadata always describe set cells order.

title: The SpatialCellData Object
text: Use CreateSpatialObject() already counts matrix coordinate table:
code: library(phenoscapR)  set.seed(1) n <- 200 counts <- matrix(   abs(rnorm(n * 4, mean = 500, sd = 200)),   nrow = n,   dimnames = list(NULL, c("CD3", "CD8", "CD20", "PanCK")) ) coords <- data.frame(x = runif(n, 0, 1000), y = runif(n, 0, 1000))  obj <- CreateSpatialObject(counts, coords, project = "demo") obj #> A SpatialCellData object #>   200 cells across 1 sample #>   Markers: CD3, CD8, CD20, PanCK  #>   Normalised: FALSE  #>   Project: demo

title: The SpatialCellData Object
text: ReadSpatial() reads one segmentation CSVs returns SpatialCellData directly. auto-detects delimiter, byte-order marks, three common layouts (QuPath full export, QuPath minimal, flat segmentation tables), parses sample_id per file.
code: # A single file obj <- ReadSpatial("path/to/segmentation.csv", sample_id = "sample1")  # A whole directory (sample_id defaults to each file's name) obj <- ReadSpatial("path/to/csv_dir/")

title: The SpatialCellData Object
text: SpatialCellData follows matrix-style [cells, markers] subsetting. indices optional. Subsetting carries every slot — counts, normalised data, coordinates, metadata, reductions — along together, downstream analysis subset always self-consistent.
code: # By cells: keep one sample a <- spe[spe$sample_id == "tonsil_A", ] dim(a) #> [1] 320   8  # By cells: keep just the B-cell follicle follicle <- spe[spe$phenotype == "B cell", ] NCells(follicle) #> [1] 160  # By markers: keep two channels spe[, c("CD3", "CD20")] #> A SpatialCellData object #>   640 cells across 2 samples #>   Markers: CD3, CD20  #>   Normalised: TRUE  #>   Phenotypes: 6  #>   Project: phenoscapR example (tonsil, simulated)

title: Advanced Spatial Analysis
text: Beyond nearest neighbours density, phenoscapR provides suite point- pattern statistics asking cells spatially organised: Neighbourhood enrichment — phenotype pairs co-localise chance? Ripley’s K / L — clustering dispersion across many scales Pair correlation function — clustering specific distance Moran’s — spatial autocorrelation continuous marker Quadrat analysis — quick chi-squared test spatial randomness Cross nearest-neighbour distance — directed proximity two phenotypes Delaunay network — cell-contact graph Expression clustering — marker-defined communities, ignoring position

title: Advanced Spatial Analysis
text: statistics describe single point pattern one observation window. Pooling several tissues compute distances across samples return nonsense, phenoscapR refuses multi-sample objects functions — subset one sample first. (Per-cell summaries like FindNeighbours(), CellDensity(), InteractionMatrix() sample-aware need subsetting.)
code: library(phenoscapR) data(phenoscapR_example)  spe <- phenoscapR_example spe@meta_data$phenotype <- spe@meta_data$phenotype_true  # A single tissue section. a <- spe[spe$sample_id == "tonsil_A", ] a #> A SpatialCellData object #>   320 cells across 1 sample #>   Markers: CD3, CD4, CD8, CD20, CD68, ... (8 total)  #>   Normalised: FALSE  #>   Phenotypes: 6  #>   Project: phenoscapR example (tonsil, simulated)

title: Advanced Spatial Analysis
text: permutation test: shuffles phenotype labels many times asks whether phenotype pair observed neighbours (positive z) less (negative z) often shuffles. planted B-cell follicle shows strong B–B self-enrichment.
code: ne <- NeighbourhoodEnrichment(a, radius = 40, n_perm = 199, seed = 1) ne[order(-ne$z_score), ][1:6, ] #> <phenoscapR> Neighbourhood enrichment (permutation test) #>   top co-localised pairs (by z-score): #>         from          to   z_score       p_value #>       B cell      B cell 24.996390 6.691699e-138 #>        T reg    T helper  9.851029  6.784551e-23 #>     T helper       T reg  9.851029  6.784551e-23 #>     T helper T cytotoxic  8.315542  9.133401e-17 #>  T cytotoxic    T helper  8.315542  9.133401e-17

title: Advanced Spatial Analysis
text: RipleysK() accumulates, radius r, average number cells within r, normalised intensity. complete spatial randomness K(r) = πr²; L transform makes departures easy read (L(r) > 0 means clustering). border correction removes edge bias.
code: rk <- RipleysK(a, r_seq = seq(0, 120, length.out = 40), correction = "border") head(rk) #> <phenoscapR> Ripley's K / border correction #>   6 radii from 0 to 15.4 #>   L(r) range: [0, 9.75]  (>0 clustered, <0 dispersed) #>          r        K        L  expected #> 1 0.000000   0.0000 0.000000   0.00000 #> 2 3.076923 158.7302 4.031198  29.74289 #> 3 6.153846 317.4603 3.898554 118.97156 #> 4 9.230769 674.6032 5.422997 267.68600  with(rk, {   plot(r, L, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#3366cc",        xlab = "r", ylab = "L(r)  (>0 = clustered)",        main = "Ripley's L, border-corrected")   abline(h = 0, lty = 2) })

title: Advanced Spatial Analysis
text: PairCorrelation() scale-resolved companion Ripley’s K: g(r) > 1 means pairs distance r expected, g(r) < 1 means inhibition.
code: pcf <- PairCorrelation(a, r_seq = seq(5, 120, length.out = 40)) with(pcf, {   plot(r, g, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#cc3366",        xlab = "r", ylab = "g(r)", main = "Pair correlation function")   abline(h = 1, lty = 2) })

title: Advanced Spatial Analysis
text: Spatial autocorrelation continuous variable. lineage marker like CD20, concentrated follicle, autocorrelates strongly (well expectation, tiny p-value).
code: MoransI(a, feature = "CD20", radius = 50) #> <phenoscapR> Moran's I spatial autocorrelation #>   I = 1.0886   (expected -0.0031 under no autocorrelation) #>   z = 34.557, p = 1.13e-261 #>   significant positive autocorrelation (clustered)

title: Advanced Spatial Analysis
text: fast omnibus test: tile window nx × ny grid, count cells per tile, compare uniform expectation chi-squared test. variance--mean ratio (VMR) exceeds 1 clustered patterns.
code: qa <- QuadratAnalysis(a, nx = 5, ny = 5) qa[c("chi_sq", "p_value", "VMR")] #> $chi_sq #> [1] 367.8125 #>  #> $p_value #> [1] 2.927953e-63 #>  #> $VMR #> [1] 15.32552

title: Advanced Spatial Analysis
text: cell phenotype , distance nearest cell phenotype — directed measure close one population sits another. returns one distance per source cell.
code: d_help_to_b <- CrossNNDistance(a, from = "T helper", to = "B cell") summary(d_help_to_b) #>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.  #>   46.52  168.36  203.95  233.43  313.92  484.20

title: Advanced Spatial Analysis
text: Delaunay triangulation approximates cells physically touch. Capping edge length max_edge drops long edges span empty space.
code: a <- DelaunayNetwork(a, max_edge = 60) nrow(a@spatial$delaunay_edges) #> [1] 661 SpatialNetworkPlot(a)

title: Advanced Spatial Analysis
text: Cluster cells normalised marker profiles, independent position, look clusters fall tissue.
code: a <- ExpressionClusters(a, k = 6) table(a$expr_cluster) #>  #>  1  2  3  4  5  6  #> 45 67 31 59 38 80 CellMap(a, colour_by = "expr_cluster")

text: run kd-tree search engine, scale large sections; 20,000-cell tissue completes statistic seconds.

title: Visualisation Gallery
text: Every phenoscapR plotting function returns ggplot object, can add themes, facets, annotations usual, draw global palette system consistent colours across figure panel. gallery shows one bundled example data.
code: library(phenoscapR) library(ggplot2) data(phenoscapR_example)  obj <- phenoscapR_example obj@meta_data$phenotype <- obj@meta_data$phenotype_true obj <- NormaliseData(obj, method = "zscore")  # A single tissue for the spatial maps. a <- obj[obj$sample_id == "tonsil_A", ] # Cell subsetting invalidates cached local density; compute it on this tissue. a <- CellDensity(a, radius = 40) markers <- c("CD20", "CD3", "CD8", "PanCK")

title: Advanced Capabilities
text: Every spatial statistic returns classed object tidy print one-line autoplot(), still behaving like underlying data frame.

code: obj <- ExpressionClusters(obj, k = 6, method = "gmm") #> Package 'mclust' version 6.1.3 #> Type 'citation("mclust")' for citing this R package in publications. AnnotateClusters(obj, add_column = FALSE) #>            1            2            3            4            5            6  #>  "CD20Ki67+"    "CD8CD3+" "PanCKKi67+"      "CD68+"    "CD4CD3+"  "FoxP3CD4+"

title: Advanced Capabilities
text: Compare phenotype proportions across conditions, sample unit replication.
code: obj@meta_data$arm <- ifelse(obj$sample_id == "tonsil_A", "ctrl", "treat") DifferentialAbundance(obj, condition = "arm") #> Warning: Some conditions have fewer than 2 samples; p-values are unreliable. #> <phenoscapR> Differential abundance (wilcox test) #>   conditions: ctrl vs treat #>   0 of 6 phenotypes differ at p_adj < 0.05 #>    phenotype mean_ctrl mean_treat statistic p_value p_adj #>       B cell  0.250000   0.250000       0.5       1     1 #>   Epithelial  0.281250   0.281250       0.5       1     1 #>   Macrophage  0.118750   0.118750       0.5       1     1 #>  T cytotoxic  0.140625   0.140625       0.5       1     1 #>     T helper  0.171875   0.171875       0.5       1     1 #>        T reg  0.037500   0.037500       0.5       1     1

title: Getting Started with phenoscapR
text: phenoscapR takes raw multiplexed-imaging cell-segmentation table way publication-ready spatial statistics figures. workflow mirrors way single-cell analysts already think: Read segmentation output SpatialCellData object Quality-control cells area intensity Normalise marker intensities Phenotype cells marker thresholds Analyse spatial arrangement phenotypes Visualise every step Every function comes two flavours: high-level S4 interface takes returns SpatialCellData object (used throughout vignette), low-level data.table interface (read_spatial(), qc_filter(), …) scripting. share one compute engine, results identical.

title: Getting Started with phenoscapR
text: package ships phenoscapR_example, fully synthetic two-sample tonsil assay planted spatial niches (B-cell follicle, overlapping T-cell zone, epithelial region, scattered macrophages). lets every example run without downloading anything. carries 640 cells across two samples eight markers, plus phenotype_true column recording ground-truth population cell: Reading data. practice start ReadSpatial("segmentation.csv") (directory CSVs). phenoscapR auto-detects QuPath full/minimal exports flat segmentation tables. See vignette("phenoscapR-02-object-model") object model import details.
code: library(phenoscapR) data(phenoscapR_example)  phenoscapR_example #> A SpatialCellData object #>   640 cells across 2 samples #>   Markers: CD3, CD4, CD8, CD20, CD68, ... (8 total)  #>   Normalised: FALSE  #>   Project: phenoscapR example (tonsil, simulated) table(phenoscapR_example$sample_id, phenoscapR_example$phenotype_true) #>            #>            B cell Epithelial Macrophage T cytotoxic T helper T reg #>   tonsil_A     80         90         38          45       55    12 #>   tonsil_B     80         90         38          45       55    12

title: Getting Started with phenoscapR
text: QCFilter() removes implausibly small large cells , optionally, cells outside intensity band. work copy original stays intact. Use QCPlot() inspect kept two metadata columns:
code: obj <- QCFilter(phenoscapR_example, min_area = 20, max_area = 1000) obj #> A SpatialCellData object #>   640 cells across 2 samples #>   Markers: CD3, CD4, CD8, CD20, CD68, ... (8 total)  #>   Normalised: FALSE  #>   Project: phenoscapR example (tonsil, simulated) obj <- CellDensity(obj, radius = 40) QCPlot(obj, x = "cell_area", y = "density", colour_by = "phenotype_true")

title: Getting Started with phenoscapR
text: NormaliseData() rescales marker. "zscore" centres scales unit variance; "minmax" maps [0, 1]; "quantile" rank-based.

title: Getting Started with phenoscapR
text: Assign phenotypes thresholding normalised markers. data z-scored, threshold 1 means “least one standard deviation marker’s mean”. PhenotypeCells() builds composite labels CD3+/CD4+. rest vignette use curated ground-truth populations figures stay easy read: CompositionPlot() shows phenotype proportions per sample:
code: obj <- PhenotypeCells(obj, thresholds = list(   CD20 = 1, CD3 = 1, CD8 = 1, CD4 = 1, CD68 = 1, PanCK = 1, FoxP3 = 1 )) head(PhenotypeSummary(obj)) #>   sample_id   phenotype count proportion #> 1  tonsil_A    Negative    53   0.165625 #> 2  tonsil_A   CD3+/CD8+    20   0.062500 #> 3  tonsil_A       CD20+    63   0.196875 #> 4  tonsil_A       CD68+    36   0.112500 #> 5  tonsil_A        CD3+    11   0.034375 #> 6  tonsil_A CD4+/FoxP3+     6   0.018750 obj@meta_data$phenotype <- obj@meta_data$phenotype_true CompositionPlot(obj, group_by = "sample_id")

title: Getting Started with phenoscapR
text: CellMap() workhorse plot — every cell drawn tissue position, coloured phenotype. Spatial structure (follicle, T-cell zone) immediately visible.  Colour instead continuous marker FeaturePlot():
code: tonsil_a <- obj[obj$sample_id == "tonsil_A", ] CellMap(tonsil_a) FeaturePlot(tonsil_a, features = c("CD20", "CD3", "PanCK"))

text: InteractionMatrix() counts, per sample, often phenotype pair sits within radius one another versus random mixing predict. score log2(observed / expected) — positive means attraction, negative means avoidance. Neighbours never counted across samples.

what: Exact Allocation Tests of Independent Patient Endpoints — ExactPatientTests
title: Exact Allocation Tests of Independent Patient Endpoints — ExactPatientTests
text: Enumerates every allocation declared group sizes. statistic mean minus mean B; two-sided p value fraction absolute statistic least observed absolute statistic minus 1e-12. requires exchangeability null. Observational confounding, paired designs stratified randomisation addressed test. Repeated images must aggregated one endpoint per patient beforehand.

title: Exact Allocation Tests of Independent Patient Endpoints — ExactPatientTests

title: Exact Allocation Tests of Independent Patient Endpoints — ExactPatientTests
text: endpoints Data frame character endpoint_id, patient_id, numeric value, logical eligible. one row per endpoint patient. NA values eligibility mark unavailable observations; NaN infinite values rejected. Extra columns ignored. design Data frame character contrast_id, patient_id, group (exactly "" "B"). patient occurs per contrast; groups must nonempty. Patients can belong multiple contrasts. hypotheses Data frame unique character hypothesis_id character endpoint_id, contrast_id, family_id. Every declared row, including unavailable tests, remains result family count. missingness "require_complete" supported. expected patients must finite eligible endpoint values. patient dropped. max_allocations Positive integer ceiling exhaustive allocations, one million. Exceeding fails rather using approximation.

title: Exact Allocation Tests of Independent Patient Endpoints — ExactPatientTests
text: data frame registry, expected/evaluable group sizes, mean_difference, p_value, allocation count, probability grid step, status. Grid step resolution bound, guaranteed attainable minimum two-sided p value. Unavailable effects p values remain NA.

title: phenoscapR 0.1.1
text: Major feature release: higher-order spatial structure, unsupervised phenotyping, differential testing, platform readers, ecosystem interop. Cellular neighbourhoods / niches (CellularNeighbourhoods()): cluster cells phenotype composition local neighbourhood. Spatial domains (SpatialDomains()): partition tissue regions coherent, spatially smoothed expression. Unsupervised phenotyping: ExpressionClusters() gains Gaussian mixture-model option (method = "gmm", via mclust), AnnotateClusters() names clusters enriched markers. Differential abundance (DifferentialAbundance()): per-sample phenotype proportions compared across conditions (Wilcoxon / t / Kruskal-Wallis), BH-adjusted p-values. Platform readers: ReadMatrixCoords() general expression-plus- coordinates layout, ReadXenium(), ReadCosMx(), ReadMERSCOPE() presetting vendor’s cell-level column names. Ecosystem interop: as_Seurat(), as_SpatialExperiment(), as_SpatialCellData() convert Seurat / SpatialExperiment.

title: phenoscapR 0.1.1
text: Deeper, rigorous statistics. RipleysK() gains "translation" edge correction (pair weighted inverse window/translate overlap) – rigorous estimator rectangular windows, alongside existing "none" reduced-sample "border". MoransI() gains weight schemes (weights = "binary", "row"-standardised, "idw" inverse-distance) permutation p-value (n_perm), reported via method field. Non-binary weights use permutation test automatically. InteractionMatrix() gains permutation null (method = "permutation", n_perm) shuffles phenotype labels within sample adds z_score p_value columns. PCA now retains variance loadings: VarianceExplained() returns percent variance per component ScreePlot() visualises . translation sweep Moran weighting exercised direct references test suite.

title: phenoscapR 0.1.1

title: phenoscapR 0.1.1
text: Robustness scalability hardening. Delaunay fallback (used deldir absent) longer builds O(n^2) distance matrix; now uses kd-tree k-nearest-neighbour engine. Ripley’s K pair correlation function longer materialise full pairwise-distance set. Counting streamed kd-tree blocks folded difference array radius grid — bounded memory, search cap seeded local density avoid re-queries. Reader / CreateSpatialObject() robustness: unnamed marker matrices get stable default names -NA marker columns dropped warning; ReadSpatial() now shares handling. Duplicate marker names remain hard error (renaming mask labelling mistake). Added large-n backend-equivalence regression tests.

text: Spatial statistics now sample-aware: interaction_matrix() friends never count neighbours across samples, single-window statistics (RipleysK(), MoransI(), QuadratAnalysis(), PairCorrelation(), NeighbourhoodEnrichment(), CrossNNDistance()) refuse multi-sample objects informative error. DelaunayNetwork() builds real Delaunay triangulation via deldir (Suggests) instead -pairs placeholder, max_edge cap. Ripley’s K gains reduced-sample border correction. Added input validation friendly errors throughout (NA coordinates, degenerate samples, missing phenotype/marker columns). Fixed colour palette system: unsupported palette names now fall back default instead erroring; advertised palettes limited backend actually provides.

text: neighbour queries route shared kd-tree search engine (RANN, Suggests) exact, memory-bounded base-R fallback, replacing per-function O(n^2) distance matrices. title: phenoscapR 0.1.1
text: Fixed selected key names collapse, sep ... grouped summaries rank correlations, retaining duplicate-ID validation. Shared key validation now rejects matrix-valued keys across public consumers. Added ContrastGroupedRanks() descriptive grouped Cliff deltas explicit arm missingness policies, complete registries exact available pair counts without allocating cross-pair matrices. Fixed sorting native-encoded non-ASCII keys disjoint edge counts, grouped overlap contrasts exact patient tests preserving returned keys numerical results. Added CountRadiusSets() ID-keyed full-frame radius counts explicit reference sets, complete query outputs, required numerical search envelope, installed backend fingerprints. Initial release. Read single-cell spatial biology data read_spatial(). Quality control qc_filter(). Marker normalisation normalise_markers(). Cell phenotyping phenotype_cells() summarise_phenotypes(). Spatial analysis: nearest_neighbours(), cell_density(), interaction_matrix(), spatial_clusters(). Visualisation: plot_cell_map(), plot_density(), plot_heatmap(), plot_interactions().
